items.title: Houston Person Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995…
items.q: Roosevelt speeches, Churchill, Winston Churchill, the way they could speak to the guy on the lowest level

ctx.x: And some of the great orators past. I bought a book of speeches, but these were just great speakers up to the 60’s, and they all had that fire, you know, you go back to some of the

Roosevelt speeches, Churchill, Winston Churchill, the way they could speak to the guy on the lowest level, and to the person on the highest level, and they had that ability to change vocabularies, change words, and use inflections that would influence either crowd. And a musician has to do that too in a certain sense, by learning to read his audience. And sometimes your audience is deceptive. You know you get a bunch of people in tuxedos and you gear your music to a certain way. And that’s not really what they…

You know you mentioned changing inflection, and there’s a concept that I teach in my classes called significant tone. In other words, from African American community, like if you went to a black Baptist or black Pentecostal church, and you got up to sing “Amazing Grace,” and you sing it straight, and I heard this happen in a church one time, a girl got up and sang it straight cause she was worried about, oh, what will people think.
